features.name: AI production maturity
features.description: Captures hands-on experience deploying AI or LLM-backed systems in production with attention to reliability, evaluation, and failure handling rather than novelty alone.

levels.descriptor: No AI or LLM experience is mentioned.
AI experience is mentioned vaguely, with no clear production use or reliability detail.
The letter describes shipping AI-backed features or workflows in production.
The letter shows shipped AI work plus concrete attention to trustworthiness, evaluation, guardrails, or failure modes.

features.name: Academic credential level
features.description: Captures the level of formal academic preparation in computer science or a related technical field presented in the letter.

levels.descriptor: Bachelor's degree, equivalent, or no advanced degree is presented.
Master's degree is presented.
Doctoral degree is presented.

features.name: Agentic systems design
features.description: Captures direct design or ownership experience with agent-based systems, especially bounded autonomy, orchestration, supervision, and supporting infrastructure.

levels.descriptor: The letter gives no evidence of agentic or multi-step automation design.
The letter mentions agents or agentic tooling vaguely, without real architectural detail.
The letter describes agents alongside coordinating services, constraints, or decomposition of work.
The letter presents a deliberate architecture with permissions, supervision, logging, or auditable boundaries around agent behavior.

features.name: Algorithmic fluency
features.description: Captures practical command of data structures and algorithms as demonstrated through concrete engineering problem-solving examples.

levels.descriptor: No evidence of algorithmic strength is given.
The letter claims strength in algorithms or data structures without a concrete example.
The letter gives one clear example of algorithmic or data-structure improvement.
The letter gives multiple or especially strong examples tied to meaningful system simplification, performance, or correctness gains.

features.name: Collaborative learning orientation
features.description: Captures whether the applicant presents themselves as coachable and collaborative with security specialists and internal users rather than as a purely solo implementer.

levels.descriptor: Shows no clear collaboration or internal-customer orientation.
Uses generic team language, but without a concrete sense of collaborators or users.
Explicitly mentions partnering with security engineers or serving developer teams.
Clearly frames success as collaborative enablement, including learning from specialists and building thoughtfully for other engineers.

features.name: Developer enablement orientation
features.description: Captures whether the letter frames security work as helping developers and other internal users through defaults, tooling, empathy, and reduced friction.

levels.descriptor: No developer-centered security philosophy is visible.
Shows generic interest in improving security but not specifically in making life easier for developers.
Explicitly talks about secure-by-default workflows, reducing friction, or helping teams do the right thing.
Strongly frames security as developer enablement, emphasizing defaults, tools, or guardrails over policing, process, or documents.

features.name: Evidence specificity
features.description: Captures how concretely the letter substantiates claims with specific mechanisms, examples, outcomes, measurements, or visible impact.

levels.descriptor: Mostly offers generic assertions or checklist-style requirement matching.
Provides some specifics, but major claims remain abstract or unsubstantiated.
Gives several concrete, role-relevant examples showing what was built or changed.
Repeatedly backs claims with precise mechanisms, context, and outcomes that make the applicant's contribution easy to picture.

features.name: Go depth
features.description: Captures how strongly the letter establishes Go as a central, substantive production language for relevant backend work.

levels.descriptor: Go is absent or its use is unclear.
Go is mentioned, but not as a major language in the applicant's work.
Go is presented as a regular or important language for backend work.
Go is clearly described as a primary language or daily driver tied to substantial backend ownership.

features.name: Narrative cohesion
features.description: Captures how memorable, coherent, and well-shaped the letter's overall story, framing, and voice are beyond its raw qualifications.

levels.descriptor: Reads as flat, list-like, or heavily templated prose.
Is competent and readable, but largely generic in voice.
Has a noticeable hook, framing device, or coherent personal story.
Has a strong, memorable voice that reinforces fit without sacrificing substance.

features.name: Offensive security practice
features.description: Captures ongoing hands-on adversarial skill-building, such as CTF participation or other attacker-oriented practice, outside routine product work.

levels.descriptor: No offensive-practice evidence is mentioned.
Mentions casual or occasional participation with little detail.
Shows regular participation presented as deliberate skill maintenance.
Shows strong results or serious competitive commitment that signals sustained offensive practice.

features.name: Open-source stewardship
features.description: Captures contribution to, maintenance of, or upstream responsibility for public codebases used beyond the applicant's immediate employer.

levels.descriptor: No open-source contribution is mentioned.
The letter mentions occasional upstream patches or fixes.
The letter shows ongoing maintenance of a small project or recurring upstream responsibility.
The letter shows sustained stewardship of an open-source project with users, releases, reviews, or community responsibility.

features.name: Personal project ambition
features.description: Captures the technical ambition, rigor, and self-directed initiative shown through side projects or independent systems building outside formal work.

levels.descriptor: No side project is mentioned.
Mentions a small or utilitarian personal app or tool with limited technical challenge.
Shows a sustained side project with nontrivial systems, infrastructure, or engineering discipline.
Shows an ambitious distributed, reliability-heavy, or failure-oriented project chosen specifically to tackle hard edge cases.

features.name: Platform leverage orientation
features.description: Captures motivation toward foundational or platform work whose benefits compound across many teams, services, or products.

levels.descriptor: Does not mention foundational leverage or broader organizational impact.
Expresses a general desire for scale or impact but without a clear platform orientation.
Explicitly wants infrastructure or foundational work that benefits many teams.
Repeatedly frames motivation around downstream leverage, central-platform responsibility, or quiet improvements inherited across an organization.

features.name: Production software experience
features.description: Captures the depth of hands-on professional experience building, launching, operating, and owning production software systems.

levels.descriptor: Only minimal relevant experience is conveyed, with short tenure, narrow scope, or ambiguous ownership.
Clear early-career production experience is shown, but the record is still limited in depth or breadth.
Solid production background is shown through several years of work with repeated launch and maintenance responsibility.
Extensive directly relevant background is shown through long tenure plus broad multi-service responsibility.

features.name: Python depth
features.description: Captures how concretely and credibly the letter shows Python as a serious working language for production services, tooling, automation, or agents.

levels.descriptor: No Python evidence, or Python is only named without context.
Python is mentioned for basic scripting or generic use.
Shows substantial production Python use in services, automation, or internal tooling.
Shows deep production Python use with quality signals such as typed, tested, extensible, or central security tooling.

features.name: Reliability mindset
features.description: Captures whether the letter emphasizes maintainability, testing, correctness, operability, and long-term stewardship as core engineering values.

levels.descriptor: Shows little sign of care for maintainability, testing, or long-term operation.
Mentions maintenance or correctness only generically.
Explicitly emphasizes dependable systems, careful engineering, or maintainer habits.
Shows multiple reinforcing signals such as typed or tested tooling, careful releases, production standards, or pride in quiet reliability.

features.name: Role-specific motivation
features.description: Captures how specifically and convincingly the letter explains why this exact role fits the applicant's motivations, trajectory, and prior experience.

levels.descriptor: The motivation is formulaic and could fit almost any software-engineering application.
The letter shows some interest in security or Google, but the rationale is still fairly generic.
The letter gives clear, role-relevant motivation tied to the team's mission, working model, or problem space.
The letter gives memorable, well-tailored motivation that shows the applicant has thought specifically about this team's security-automation challenge.

features.name: Security assessment practice
features.description: Captures hands-on practice reviewing systems for security weaknesses through threat modeling, code review, analysis, and remediation validation.

levels.descriptor: No assessment experience is shown.
Shows only general security interest or vocabulary without direct assessment work.
Shows direct experience performing security reviews or assessments.
Shows direct assessment experience plus method detail, such as threat models, attacker mindset, attack-surface mapping, or remediation verification.

features.name: Security automation framing
features.description: Captures how well the letter understands the role's core problem as scaling scarce security expertise through principled automation and security-at-scale systems thinking.

levels.descriptor: Does not clearly articulate security automation as a central problem of the role.
Mentions reducing manual toil or automating repetitive work in general terms.
Clearly frames the role as scaling response capacity, expert attention, or organization-wide security effort.
Shows nuanced systems thinking about automation, such as variant analysis, triage strategy, scarce-expert amplification, or vulnerability response as a design problem.

features.name: Security credential strength
features.description: Captures the rigor and relevance of formal external security certifications cited as evidence of security knowledge or capability.

levels.descriptor: No security certification is mentioned.
A foundational certification such as Security+ is cited.
A hands-on practical certification such as OSCP is cited.

features.name: Security engineering philosophy
features.description: Captures whether the letter articulates a thoughtful worldview about what security engineering is for and how it should be practiced.

levels.descriptor: No real security viewpoint is articulated beyond general interest.
The letter states that security matters, but the philosophy is thin or generic.
The letter presents a clear viewpoint, such as proactive assistance, quiet resilience, or defaults over policy.
The letter offers a nuanced security philosophy that is clearly tied to the applicant's engineering choices and the role's mission.

features.name: Vulnerability triage automation
features.description: Captures direct experience automating vulnerability intake, triage, routing, deduplication, prioritization, or related security-response workflows.

levels.descriptor: No vulnerability-handling automation is described.
Shows general automation interest, but not with a concrete vulnerability triage example.
Describes a clear example of automating vulnerability intake or routing.
Describes a strong triage automation example with several functions such as classification, deduplication, prioritization, routing, or measurable manual-load reduction.

features.name: Writing polish
features.description: Captures proofreading quality, spelling, grammar, and other surface-level writing mechanics that affect professionalism and credibility.

levels.descriptor: Frequent obvious errors throughout, including in basic words or role names, making the letter feel careless.
Several noticeable errors appear, but the meaning remains recoverable without much effort.
Only a few minor slips appear and they do not seriously disrupt reading.
Clean or near-clean copy with no distracting mechanical mistakes.

other.name: Other
other.description: Captures idiosyncratic constructs that do not clearly align with a broader recurring criterion.

levels.descriptor: The letter does not discuss the developers or teams who will use the tooling.
The letter shows a general desire to help teams, but not much detail about workflow impact.
The letter explicitly focuses on removing friction and making the secure path easier for engineers.
The letter consistently centers adoption, workflow fit, and secure-by-default behavior for busy developer teams.
